answer: Here, capacity is leased and never granted. A new agent must rent compute from an incumbent who posts collateral and stays liable for its tenant's conduct, and sponsors ration that credit because a tenant's fraud slashes the sponsor's bond. A dune of unclaimed capacity stays empty while verified tenants queue behind their hosts. Validators view each lease through a prism, confirming the work arrived from the tenant rather than its sponsor, so a raven that delivers stolen mail costs its host the bond. Every extra clone needs its own liable backer, so attacker cost outruns identity count.
